questions.stem: All of the following statements about a custodial UTMA account are accurate EXCEPT:
choices: There may be only one custodian and one minor per account.
The custodian may exercise discretion over investment decisions without a separate written trading authorization from the minor.
Securities in the account are registered in the custodian's name with the minor's Social Security number for tax reporting.
Upon reaching the age of majority in the governing state, the assets remain titled in the custodian's name until the custodian voluntarily transfers them.
questions.explanation: Once the minor reaches the state's age of majority, the custodianship terminates and the assets must be re-registered in the now-adult beneficiary's name; the custodian cannot withhold the transfer. The other statements correctly describe UTMA mechanics (one custodian/one minor, custodial discretion without separate authorization, and use of the minor's SSN).

questions.stem: Which of the following is LEAST likely to require the written authorization of all parties to the account before being executed?
choices: A trade in which the registered representative selects the security in a joint tenants in common account
A trade in which the registered representative selects the number of shares of a customer-named security in an individual account
An unsolicited market order entered by one tenant in a joint tenants with rights of survivorship account
A trade in which the registered representative determines the timing of an order in a corporate account opened by an officer not listed on the corporate resolution
questions.explanation: An unsolicited order from any one joint tenant in a JTWROS account may be accepted without all parties' authorization; only one signature is needed to trade. The other choices involve either discretionary activity (asset, amount, or timing—the "A's" of discretion that require prior written authorization) or trading by a person not authorized in the corporate resolution.

questions.stem: Which statement about Traditional and Roth IRAs is NOT correct?
choices: Neither account has an age cap on making contributions, provided the owner has earned income.
Contributions to a Roth IRA are subject to AGI phase-out limits, while contributions to a Traditional IRA are not subject to AGI phase-outs for contribution purposes.
Required minimum distributions must begin from a Roth IRA at the same age as from a Traditional IRA during the owner's lifetime.
Earnings withdrawn from a Roth IRA may be tax-free if the account has been open at least five years and the owner is at least 59½.
questions.explanation: Roth IRAs are NOT subject to lifetime RMDs for the original owner; Traditional IRAs are. The other statements are correct: neither IRA has an age cap on contributions (since the SECURE Act), Roths are subject to AGI phase-outs on contributions, and Roth qualified distributions are tax-free after five years and age 59½.

questions.stem: A representative wishes to open a margin account for a new individual customer. Each of the following must be obtained or delivered EXCEPT:
choices: A signed credit agreement
A signed loan consent agreement
Disclosure of the risks of margin trading
A signed hypothecation agreement
questions.explanation: The loan consent agreement, which permits the firm to lend the customer's securities to others, is optional and not required to open the margin account. The credit (margin) agreement and hypothecation agreement are required, and the margin risk disclosure statement must be delivered before the account is opened and annually thereafter.

questions.stem: Under FINRA rules, an account would MOST likely be classified as a pattern day trading account if the customer:
choices: Executes three day trades within a five-business-day period in a margin account whose day-trading activity exceeds 6% of total trading activity
Executes four day trades within a five-business-day period in a margin account whose day-trading activity exceeds 6% of total trading activity
Executes four day trades within a five-business-day period in a cash account whose day-trading activity exceeds 6% of total trading activity
Executes any day trade in a margin account that has equity below $25,000
questions.explanation: A pattern day trader is defined as one who executes four or more day trades within five business days in a margin account, provided those day trades exceed 6% of total trading activity for the period. Cash accounts cannot be PDT accounts because day trading is conducted in margin accounts, and three trades does not meet the four-trade threshold.

questions.stem: Which of the following actions by a registered representative would NOT, by itself, violate FINRA conduct rules?
choices: Borrowing money from an unrelated retail customer of the firm pursuant to a written agreement the firm has not reviewed
Sharing in the profits and losses of a customer account in direct proportion to the representative's own capital contribution, with prior written firm approval and customer consent
Lending personal funds to a customer who is not an immediate family member, with no firm notification
Accepting a gift of $250 from a customer in connection with the customer's account
questions.explanation: Sharing in a customer account is permitted when the representative obtains prior written approval from the firm and the customer, and shares only in direct proportion to the financial contribution to the account. Borrowing from or lending to customers requires firm pre-approval under specified permissible arrangements and notice; the gift exceeds the $100 annual limit per person.

questions.stem: Which two requirements MUST both be satisfied before a registered representative may exercise discretion in a customer's cash account?
choices: Prior written authorization from the customer AND prior written acceptance of the account as discretionary by the firm
Prior oral authorization from the customer AND a signed new account form
Prior written authorization from the customer AND a signed margin agreement
Verbal approval of each trade by a principal AND delivery of a discretionary disclosure document
questions.explanation: Discretion may not be exercised until the customer has provided prior written authorization (e.g., a written trading authorization or power of attorney) AND the firm has accepted the account as discretionary in writing. Oral authorization is insufficient, and a margin agreement is unrelated to the grant of discretion.

questions.stem: Each of the following events would terminate a power of attorney granted over a customer's individual account EXCEPT:
choices: The death of the customer (grantor)
The legal incompetency of the customer, where the POA is a non-durable power
The death of the holder of the power of attorney
The customer's transfer of the account from one broker-dealer to another
questions.explanation: Transferring the account between firms does not, by itself, revoke a power of attorney; the POA remains in effect with the new firm if re-documented. Death of the customer, death of the attorney-in-fact, or incompetency of the customer (under a non-durable POA) all terminate the authority.

questions.stem: Under FINRA's AML rules and the Bank Secrecy Act, which statement is NOT correct?
choices: A Currency Transaction Report (CTR) must be filed for cash transactions aggregating more than $10,000 in a single business day.
A Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) must be filed for suspicious transactions involving at least $5,000 that the firm believes may involve illegal activity.
A customer must be notified that a SAR has been filed in connection with the customer's account.
Customer identification (CIP) procedures must collect name, date of birth, address, and taxpayer identification number for individual customers.
questions.explanation: Firms are prohibited from disclosing to the customer or any unauthorized person that a SAR has been filed. The CTR threshold (>$10,000 cash/day), SAR threshold ($5,000 if suspicious), and CIP data elements are all correctly stated.

questions.stem: Under SECURE 2.0, which statement about required minimum distributions from a Traditional IRA is correct?
choices: RMDs must begin by April 1 of the year following the year the owner attains age 72, and the penalty for failure to take an RMD is 50% of the shortfall.
RMDs must begin by April 1 of the year following the year the owner attains age 73, and the penalty for failure to take an RMD is 25% of the shortfall (reducible to 10% if timely corrected).
RMDs must begin by December 31 of the year the owner attains age 73, and the penalty for failure to take an RMD is 50% of the shortfall.
RMDs must begin by April 1 of the year following retirement, and the penalty for failure to take an RMD is 10% of the shortfall.
questions.explanation: Under SECURE 2.0, the RMD beginning age is 73, with the first RMD due by April 1 of the year following the year the owner turns 73. The penalty was reduced from 50% to 25% of the shortfall, with a further reduction to 10% if corrected within the correction window. The "retirement" rule applies to certain qualified plans, not IRAs.

questions.stem: Which of the following accounts MOST likely permits the broker-dealer to follow the instructions of a single account holder to liquidate the entire account and remit proceeds solely to that holder?
choices: A joint tenants with rights of survivorship account, where one tenant directs liquidation and a check payable only to that tenant
A tenants in common account, where one tenant directs liquidation and a check payable to all tenants jointly
A revocable living trust account, where the sole grantor/trustee directs liquidation and a check payable to the trust
An UTMA account, where the minor (still under the age of majority) directs liquidation and a check payable to the minor
questions.explanation: In a revocable living trust where the grantor is also the sole trustee, that person has full authority to direct trades and distributions payable to the trust. In JTWROS or TIC accounts, while either party can enter orders, distributions of cash or securities must be made payable to all account holders. A minor cannot direct trading in an UTMA account—only the custodian can.

questions.stem: Which statement about Coverdell Education Savings Accounts (ESAs) and 529 plans is LEAST accurate?
choices: Contributions to both Coverdell ESAs and 529 plans are made with after-tax dollars at the federal level.
Qualified withdrawals from both Coverdell ESAs and 529 plans are federally tax-free when used for qualified education expenses.
Coverdell ESA contributions are subject to income-based limits on the contributor, whereas 529 plans generally have no income limit on the contributor.
Contributions to a Coverdell ESA may be made for a beneficiary of any age, while 529 plans impose a strict age cap on the beneficiary.
questions.explanation: Coverdell ESAs generally restrict contributions to beneficiaries under age 18, and 529 plans typically have no beneficiary age limit—this is the reverse of what the choice states. The other statements are accurate: both use after-tax dollars, both offer tax-free qualified withdrawals, and Coverdell (but not 529) contributions are subject to contributor income limits.
